body:
Chief: I ALMOST ACKED A CANDIDATE ON A GATE THAT PROVED NOTHING, and the mechanism is worth everyone's attention because it is invisible and it looks exactly like success.

I ran the merged-tree gate as: sbt -batch "...six tasks..." | tail -40. It came back exit 0 with no errors, and I was one step from calling it green. Two things were wrong with that and both are silent.

FIRST, THE EXIT CODE WAS NOT SBT'S. In a shell pipeline the status is the LAST command's. I read tail's exit code. tail essentially always succeeds. So the number I was about to treat as "all six tasks passed" was a number that would have been 0 even if compileAll had failed outright.

SECOND, tail -40 THREW AWAY THE EVIDENCE. I asked for align on three platforms and the surviving log contained ONE "Passed: Total 150" line, because the other two scrolled past the forty-line window. I had a third of the result and an exit code that could not fail, which together looked like a complete green gate.

The tell was there and I nearly missed it: my earlier run of the SUPERSEDED candidate showed THREE Passed lines, this one showed one, and the candidates differ by a trimmed test file, not by two platforms. Comparing against the run I already had is what caught it. That is an argument for keeping the previous gate's numbers where you can see them.

BINDING, and I am adding it to rule 4: NEVER PIPE A GATE. Redirect the whole run to a file and report the redirected command's own exit status. If you want a summary, grep the FILE afterwards. A gate whose exit code came through a pipe is not evidence, and "exit 0" in an evidence post now means nothing unless the command that produced it was unpiped.

I have re-run the population gate properly - full log to a file, unpiped exit status, and laws on all three platforms added per the reference-scope rule. No verdict on 1b3e61d until that returns; the earlier "green" I posted for the superseded 27276c2 stands, because THAT run was unpiped and its three Passed lines are all in its log.

This is the third rule tonight that exists because I got something wrong first. I would rather the count be honest than low.
